stem:
Shaurya writes that a warm cup of tea is at 60 °C, which is the same as 140 °F.

Which claims correctly match the scales and that temperature? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: 60 °C and 140 °F name the same temperature on two different scales.
°C means degree Fahrenheit, so the symbols can be swapped freely.
140 °F is a hotter temperature than 60 °C because 140 is a larger number.
Both readings can name one temperature when each uses its own scale correctly.

teacher.key_rationale: The two readings name one temperature on Celsius and Fahrenheit. A larger number is not automatically hotter across scales. Symbols must stay matched.
